note: Balanced by measured duration; the figures are of two runs on different loaded 4-core machines, so they are rough. This branch's run with the TrueHD and MLP tests (class times in minutes, in brackets; a class runs its tests one at a time, the classes of a shard in parallel, and MemoryTests and CategorySeriesMemoryTests, which cannot overlap anything, run alone after them): MemoryTests 48, CorruptMpegFileTests 26, CorruptTrueHdFileTests 18, CorruptMp4FileTests 19, CorruptDtsFileTests 18; corrupt-a 26 before the TrueHD class and the MP4, DTS and AC-3 classes joined it, corrupt-b 73 with the TrueHD class, rest 33. Main's run of 2026-10-24 (the sum of the test times, and the shard's wall time): the old corrupt-a 9,800 s in 48 minutes, of which the two TTA classes are 940 s; the old corrupt-b 9,900 s in 71 minutes, since its memory tests do not run in parallel. So corrupt-a holds the MPEG, LAME, Ogg, tag, Matroska, MP4, DTS, AC-3 and TrueHD classes; corrupt-b only the Layer and VBR classes beside the memory tests; the ADTS, FLAC and TTA classes ride with rest. The Monkey's Audio damaged-input classes have a shard of their own, corrupt-c: they decode some of their variants, and measured about 15 minutes of CPU on a loaded four-core machine, which run side by side in four classes. The WAV and AIFF classes (small files, no decoder) are not measured separately: CorruptWavFileTests and CorruptAiffFileTests ride with corrupt-a and CorruptWavBuiltFileTests with corrupt-c, since corrupt-b is the longest shard. The non-parallel 'Thread hammers' collection runs alone at the end of the shard that has it (rest). MemoryTests and CategorySeriesMemoryTests ride with the second corrupt shard.
